title: "AI agents: set-up in the Claude desktop app"

```{r, include = FALSE}
# A chunk's code sits under "Show code": open when it is what the page is
# about (`fold = "open"`), closed when it only supports it (`fold = "closed"`,
# the default unless the page sets another); `fold = FALSE` shows it plain,
# and so is code of three lines or fewer.
# Its results stay outside, always shown.
.fold_src <- knitr::knit_hooks$get("source")
knitr::knit_hooks$set(source = function(x, options) {
  f <- if (is.null(options$fold)) "closed" else options$fold
  # short code -- three lines or fewer, a chunk or the part of one before
  # its next output -- is shown as it is: folded, it would hide less than
  # the fold itself takes
  if (isFALSE(f) || length(unlist(strsplit(x, "\n", fixed = TRUE))) <= 3L) {
    return(.fold_src(x, options))
  }
  paste0("\n\n<details", if (identical(f, "open")) " open", ">",
         "<summary>Show code</summary>\n\n",
         .fold_src(x, options), "\n\n</details>\n\n")
})
knitr::opts_chunk$set(fold = "open")   # this page: the code is the subject
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", eval = FALSE)
```

This page sets up the Claude desktop app's Code tab for work on rtfreporter,
tflspec or tflplanner. Read [Developing with AI agents](ai-agents.html) first:
it says what the set-up is for. Come back to that page for the workflow when
you are done.

The facts here come from Anthropic's Claude Code documentation, read on
2026-11-08 (see the links). The app's own screens change often. Where the
documentation does not show a screen, the step is marked **(to check)**.

## Open the repository

1. Clone the repository with `git`. A contributor clones a fork, a
   collaborator clones `ichirio/rtfreporter` (*Contributor vs Collaborator* in
   `CONTRIBUTING.md`).
2. In the Code tab, use the project folder control in the row under the prompt
   box, and choose the clone's folder.
3. To keep the work apart from your main checkout, turn on **Worktree** before
   you start the session. It is off by default. Then Claude works in its own Git
   worktree, under `<project-root>/.claude/worktrees/` by default.
4. Make the topic branch: ask Claude to run `git checkout -b <type>/<issue>-<slug>`
   from the right base (*Branching & collaboration* in `CONTRIBUTING.md`).
   **(To check:** whether the app has its own branch picker.**)**

Source: <https://code.claude.com/docs/en/desktop>

## The environment

The agent's commands must see the work library and the work home, not yours
([section 2 of the shared article](ai-agents.html#the-environment)).

* In the app, put `KEY=value` lines in a **saved local environment** and start
  the session from it. Put `R_LIBS_USER`, `HOME`, `R_USER_CACHE_DIR`,
  `R_USER_DATA_DIR`, `R_USER_CONFIG_DIR`, `TMP`, `TEMP`, `TMPDIR` and
  `WORK_ROOT` there. **(To check:** whether Windows paths with a drive letter
  need quoting in that editor.**)**
* The `env` block of `~/.claude/settings.json` is not a safe place: the
  documentation says Claude Code ignores some `env` values in local sessions.
* Tell the agent which R to call, by its full path, in the instruction file
  (next section).

Then ask Claude to run the check script from the shared article, with that R:

> Save the script from "The environment" as `check-env.R` outside the
> repository, run it with the project's R, and show me the output.

It must end with `Environment OK.` If it stops, fix the environment before
anything else.

Source: <https://code.claude.com/docs/en/desktop>

## Instructions

Claude Code reads `CLAUDE.md` at the start of each session. It reads `AGENTS.md`
only when there is no `CLAUDE.md` in the folder or above it (this needs Claude
Code 2.1.277 or later). This repository has an `AGENTS.md`. A short `CLAUDE.md`
that imports it keeps one source, and lets you add the Claude-specific lines:

```markdown
@AGENTS.md

## Claude Code

- Call R by its full path (the project's R), never a bare `Rscript`.
- Run the pre-PR check (`/pre-pr`) before you open a pull request.
- Do not edit `NEWS.md`, `CHANGELOG.md` or `Version:` in `DESCRIPTION`.
- Stop and ask before you push, install into a library, or delete files.
```

To confirm that the file was read, ask: "Which instructions did you load for
this repository?" The answer should name `CLAUDE.md` and `AGENTS.md`. The
Claude Code documentation describes a `/memory` command in the terminal tool.
**(To check:** whether the desktop app lists the loaded files, and where.**)**

An instruction file is context, not a lock. For a rule that must hold, use a
hook (below).

Source: <https://code.claude.com/docs/en/memory>

## Permissions

Claude asks before it edits files or runs most commands. The app has permission
modes under the prompt box: Manual, Accept edits, Plan, Auto and Bypass
permissions. For this work use **Manual** or **Accept edits**. Do not use
Bypass permissions outside a sandbox, such as a container; the documentation
says the same.

Allow the commands you run often, and deny the ones you want to decide
yourself. The rules go in `.claude/settings.json` (shared) or
`.claude/settings.local.json` (yours). The R path below is an example:

```json
{
  "permissions": {
    "allow": [
      "Bash(git status *)",
      "Bash(git diff *)",
      "Bash(git log *)",
      "Bash(\"C:/Program Files/R/R-4.6.1/bin/Rscript.exe\" *)"
    ],
    "deny": [
      "Bash(git push *)",
      "Bash(rm *)"
    ]
  }
}
```

Two cautions from the documentation. A rule matches the command as written:
`git -C . push` is not matched by `Bash(git push *)`. So treat `deny` as a
guide and use a hook for a rule that must hold. And an allowed `Rscript` can run
any R code, so allow it only after the environment check passes.

Keep these as "ask": `git push`, installing into any library other than the
work library, and deleting files. A push goes through you, as a person.

Sources: <https://code.claude.com/docs/en/permissions>,
<https://code.claude.com/docs/en/desktop>

## The pre-PR check

A **skill** is a folder with a `SKILL.md` file. A project skill lives in
`.claude/skills/<name>/SKILL.md`; commit it to share it. Local sessions in the
desktop app load personal skills from `~/.claude/skills/` and project skills
from the repository. You start it with `/<name>`. This example is
`.claude/skills/pre-pr/SKILL.md`:

```markdown
---
name: pre-pr
description: The checks to run before opening a pull request in rtfreporter, tflspec or tflplanner.
disable-model-invocation: true
---

Run these in order. Stop at the first failure and report it.

1. Run the tests of the changed area, then the whole suite in one R session
   (`testthat::test_dir()` on the installed package).
2. Run `lintr::lint_package()`. It must report 0 lints.
3. List the `pkg::` uses and `requireNamespace()` calls added in the diff, and
   check each is declared in `DESCRIPTION`.
4. If the change is in tflspec, run tflplanner's tests too.
5. Report each result in the form the pull request template asks for.

Do not edit `NEWS.md`, `CHANGELOG.md` or `Version:`.
```

`disable-model-invocation: true` means only you start it. Then type `/pre-pr`
in the prompt box. **(To check:** that `/pre-pr` appears in the desktop app's
slash menu for a project skill.**)**

Source: <https://code.claude.com/docs/en/skills>

## Checks on each edit

A **hook** is a command that Claude Code runs at a fixed point. Hooks are set
in `.claude/settings.json`. A `PreToolUse` hook runs before a tool call and
can block it with exit code 2; the message on stderr is what Claude sees. The
matcher `Edit|Write` selects file edits, and the file path is in
`tool_input.file_path`. This example refuses an edit to `NEWS.md` or
`CHANGELOG.md`, and refuses an edit to `DESCRIPTION` that touches `Version:`:

```json
{
  "hooks": {
    "PreToolUse": [
      {
        "matcher": "Edit|Write",
        "hooks": [
          {
            "type": "command",
            "command": "${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR}/.claude/hooks/protect-release-files.sh",
            "args": []
          }
        ]
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

```bash
#!/bin/bash
# .claude/hooks/protect-release-files.sh  (needs jq)
input=$(cat)
file=$(echo "$input" | jq -r '.tool_input.file_path // empty')
case "$file" in
  */NEWS.md|*/CHANGELOG.md)
    echo "A pull request never edits NEWS.md or CHANGELOG.md." >&2
    exit 2 ;;
  */DESCRIPTION)
    text=$(echo "$input" | jq -r '[.tool_input.old_string, .tool_input.new_string, .tool_input.content] | map(. // "") | join("\n")')
    if echo "$text" | grep -q '^Version:'; then
      echo "A pull request never edits Version: in DESCRIPTION." >&2
      exit 2
    fi ;;
esac
exit 0
```

A `PostToolUse` hook on the same matcher can lint a changed `.R` file, as in
the documentation's example. A `PostToolUse` hook cannot undo the edit; it only
reports back to Claude.

**(To check:** that hooks run in the desktop app's local sessions, which shell
runs them on Windows, and whether the app has a screen for them.**)** The
documentation says a worktree session reads the project's settings, hooks and
skills. If hooks do not run in your set-up, the pre-PR check and CI cover the
same rules.

Whether these hook files ship in the repository, or stay in this article, is
not decided.

Source: <https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks>

## Then

Back to [the workflow in the shared article](ai-agents.html#the-workflow):
issue, small branch, test first, pre-PR check, pull request. After you open the
pull request, the app shows it with its CI status; the documentation says this
needs the GitHub CLI (`gh`) installed and signed in.
